short: a local that's never reassigned after it's set. the only kind a lambda may capture.
the functional interface a lambda becomes, decided by where it's written: assignment, argument or cast.
a lambda that just calls one existing method, written as Class::method or expr::method.
a lazy stream step like filter or map. it only adds a stage, no work happens yet.
the stream step that pulls elements through and produces a result: toList, count, forEach.
a stream operation that can finish without seeing every element: limit, findFirst, anyMatch.
an intermediate op that remembers earlier elements: distinct, sorted, limit, skip.
turns each element into a stream of zero or more elements and splices them into one stream.
a collector that runs inside each group of another, like counting() in groupingBy.
the starting value of a reduction, one that changes nothing: 0 for +, 1 for *.
folding a stream into a container that each chunk fills privately. what collect does.
IntStream, LongStream or DoubleStream: a stream of raw numbers, no boxing.
the part of a gatherer that sees each element, pushes results downstream and can stop the stream.
the iterator a stream's source provides. it can split itself in half for parallel work.
the JVM-wide ForkJoinPool that every parallel stream shares. cores minus one threads.
